events.summary: Speaker C stated the project is to create a new remote control for a television that is original, trendy and user friendly.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: What we're aiming to do is to create a new remote control for a television

events.summary: Speaker C set the method: each member works individually first, then the group comes together for meetings.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: work individually initially and then come together for meetings

events.summary: Speaker C said the remote controls will be sold for 25 Euros each.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we're planning to sell the remote controls for twenty five Euros each

events.summary: Speaker C said the target profit is 50 million Euros, selling on the international market.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we're aiming for a profit of fifty million Euros

events.summary: Speaker C said finance estimates production costs must be at most 12.5 Euros per unit to reach the profit target.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we need production costs of maximum twelve and a half Euro

events.summary: Speaker A proposed providing features that are unique to this remote control, to meet the originality goal.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we should provide some features that are quite unique to this

events.summary: Speaker B proposed the motto we put the fashion in electronics, meaning sleek, stylish and still functional.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: the motto is um we put the fashion in electronics

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a remote with no buttons, like the new generation phones.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: where they don't actually have any buttons on them and stuff like that

events.summary: Speaker C proposed a menu-based interface.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: So perhaps some sort of menu-based thing, or

events.summary: Speaker C refined Speaker B's no-button idea: keep one button for a menu, if needed.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: It could be one button for a menu or something

events.summary: Speaker B proposed doing the functions on screen instead of buttons, because the buttons confuse people.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: rather than everybody else having to have those buttons, which just confuse them

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a sleek design with no extra parts, like the train shown on the website.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: there's no extra bits on it, the train on the website

events.summary: Speaker A proposed aiming for a high battery life, while noting batteries are not a huge problem for remote controls.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we can aim for something wi that gives a high battery life

events.summary: Speaker D objected to going too far from the usual remote controls, because new users would have learning problems.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: we shouldn't uh go like too far away from from the usual ones

events.summary: Speaker A agreed the design should fit in with familiar expectations of a remote control.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: So, i it should kind of fit in as well

events.summary: Speaker C objected that fancy websites are unusable when users cannot tell how to get in, supporting Speaker D's objection.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: that you can't access because you have no idea how to get in

events.summary: Speaker C assigned the working design task to Speaker A.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: you're looking at the working design

events.summary: Speaker C assigned the technical functions design task to Speaker D.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: you're looking at the technical functions design

events.summary: Speaker C assigned the user requirements specification to Speaker B.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: for you it's the user requirements specification, like you said
